A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RePro research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original model-training experiments, reasoning benchmark results, ablations, token-efficiency analyses, and qualitative cases in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and additionally reports efficiency-baseline token counts and training-entropy dynamics in Appendices A and C.5.

M1.justification: The proxy objective, magnitude and stability scores, entropy-based segment selection, process rewards, and RL integration remain unchanged in Section 3 and Appendix B.1.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same DeepScaleR training corpus and AIME24, AIME25, MATH500, LiveMathBench, GPQA-Diamond, MBPP, and LiveCodeBench evaluations. The new entropy analysis introduces no additional dataset, domain, or task scenario.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is retained throughout the existing experiments. Table 3 still compares against vanilla GRPO, ThinkPrune-4k, L1-Max, both Laser variants, and AdaThink; its added token column does not introduce another baseline.

E3.justification: v2 extends reported measurements with average token counts in Table 3 and entropy versus training step over approximately 200 steps in Figure 11. Existing benchmark splits, decoding settings, model configurations, and 500-step training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix C.5 and Figure 11 examine whether RePro preserves policy entropy relative to vanilla GRPO. Existing score-weight and segment-count ablations, backtracking analyses, token-efficiency plots, and case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages over 16 runs for AIME24/AIME25 and four runs for other benchmarks. v2 specifies no new seed counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Existing accuracy entries and case-study outcomes are unchanged. Table 3 adds token counts, including 12,367 for vanilla GRPO and 6,558 for RePro; Figure 11 adds entropy trajectories ending around 0.255 and above 0.27, respectively. The new Appendix A prose inconsistently gives RePro's count as 6,158.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and Equations (1)–(18) are retained. No new formal assumptions, theoretical results, proofs, or substantive derivations accompany the empirical additions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: an optimization perspective on reasoning, a dual process reward, integration with RL algorithms, and improved reasoning performance and efficiency.

C2.justification: Appendix A expands the accuracy-efficiency interpretation, and Appendix C.5 interprets higher entropy as sustained exploration and reduced premature policy collapse. New Appendix E explicitly identifies untested scaling beyond 8B parameters and unexplored applicability to subjective or difficult-to-verify problems.

D1.justification: v1 explicitly advertises available code and data. v2 retains the repository link but adds a reproducibility statement describing supplementary implementations and promising complete code upon acceptance. This changes the access description without establishing an actual availability change; Appendix B's implementation settings remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 removes ToRL and SituatedThinker from Section 5 and the references, while retaining the other cited works despite changed citation suffixes. Appendix A also expands positioning against existing efficiency methods using the new token-cost comparison.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section ordering are retained. v2 adds ethics and reproducibility statements, an appendix contents page, the entropy subsection, limitations, and an LLM-usage disclosure, alongside publication and author-header edits.

P2.justification: The document is extensively reset in the ICLR format, changing the title block, typography, text width, and figure/table sizes and placement. Figures 1–10 are retained, Figure 11 is added, and Table 3 gains a token column. Some comparison symbols in Case D.3 prose also render incorrectly.

improvement.justification: Table 3 now supports direct accuracy-versus-token-cost comparisons, while Figure 11 and explicit applicability limits modestly strengthen the paper's evidence and qualification of its conclusions. These benefits outweigh limited regressions, including the new 6,158-versus-6,558 token inconsistency and case-study typesetting errors. The method and principal benchmark results remain unchanged.
